<reason>Both sides built coherent, well-executed cases and handled the Pressure Questions round with proper A1/A2 structure. CON's central strategy—charging that PRO's "turnkey on open interfaces" collapses into CON's own case-by-case contract discipline—was sharp and repeated effectively, but PRO supplied a real conceptual rejoinder ("who delivers" vs. "who owns the locks," openness as a scored structural default rather than a negotiated afterthought) that CON never fully dismantled in Rebuttal 2 or Closing, instead mostly re-asserting the "concession" label. PRO also answered the crisis-portability and leverage pressure questions concretely (mandatory export/documented APIs, cooperative certification akin to building codes) and kept the human stakes (records following students and patients) vivid throughout, giving PRO the cleaner, more resolution-faithful path by the end.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's B4.1 answer to CON's "concession" pressure question—distinguishing turnkey delivery from vendor lock-in ownership and reframing openness as a categorical scoring default—was the pivotal exchange CON's closing never fully answered.</best_rebuttal>
